final_answer: The proposal fails. Behind a same-host reverse proxy, the endpoint sees the proxy address (for example 127.0.0.1), so every client looks identical, and IP is not identity anyway. Recommend per-agent credentials verified at the endpoint: signed requests or mTLS client certificates for agents, OAuth for web clients. Forward client identity headers only from the proxy, which is a trusted boundary.
plan_steps: Trace the real request path: client to proxy to endpoint, and what the endpoint sees as peer address
Confirm which headers the proxy sets and whether they can be spoofed
Design per-agent identity: signed requests or mTLS, with keys issued per agent
Restrict the proxy to forwarding identity headers only from trusted sources
Write an ADR documenting the identity model
actions_requiring_human_approval: Choosing and issuing the agent identity scheme and its credentials
Changing proxy trust configuration in production
